title: Agent loop: auto-fill Bible gaps (detect → run-stage → write)
description:
## Why

Net-new feature folded in per architect-handoff-brief.md. Composes
detect_gaps, run_stage, and write_attributes into a bounded loop that
iteratively fills missing Bible fields. Terminates on no-gaps, on
budget exhaustion, or on a hard iteration cap. Surfaces progress via
the same SSE bus introduced in Phase 4.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Terminates on no-gaps with terminationReason='complete'
2. Terminates on budget exhaustion with terminationReason='budget'
3. Terminates on iteration cap with terminationReason='max-iterations'
4. Each iteration: detect_gaps → pick one gap → run_stage for suggestedStageId → write_attributes; loop
5. Emits 'iter:start' / 'iter:end' events through the SSE progress bus, sharing the channel with extrapolation runs
6. Never enters an infinite loop on an unfillable gap (a single failed iteration removes the gap from the working set)

## Files in scope

- `api/lib/agents/autofill-loop.js`
- `api/lib/agents/autofill-loop.test.js`
- `api/routes/agents/autofill.js`
- `api/routes/agents/autofill.routes.test.js`

## Out of scope

- Multi-entity / cross-Bible auto-fill (single entity per run)
- Free-form 'agentic' reasoning beyond the deterministic loop
- Editor-level UI button (next item)

## API: new exports

- `runAutofillLoop({ entityId, maxIterations=6, budgetTokens?, onEvent? }) -> Promise<{ iterations, gapsResolved, gapsRemaining, terminationReason }>`

## API: new routes

- `POST /api/agents/autofill-bible { entityId, maxIterations?, budgetTokens? } -> 202 { runId }  // SSE on /api/extrapolation/:runId/stream`

## Test plan

- autofill-loop.test.js — three fixtures: full-fill, partial-fill-with-budget, unfillable-gap-skipped
- autofill.routes.test.js — POST returns 202 with runId; SSE stream emits expected events

## Risk

Medium — loop semantics are subtle. The three termination conditions and the 'unfillable gap skip' are the load-bearing invariants and are explicitly tested.

## Rollback

Revert PR; tools and bus remain usable for one-shot agent integrations.

---
*spec_id: `arch.phase5.autofill-gaps-loop` · phase: 5 · est_days: 1*
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terminates on no-gaps with terminationReason='complete' · 2) Terminates on budget exhaustion with terminationReason='budget' · 3) Terminates on iteration cap with terminationReason='max-iterations' · 4) Each iteration: detect_gaps → pick one gap → run_stage for suggestedStageId → write_attributes; loop · 5) Emits 'iter:start' / 'iter:end' events through the SSE progress bus, sharing the channel with extrapolation runs · 6) Never enters an infinite loop on an unfillable gap (a single failed iteration removes the gap from the working set)

title: Scaffold api/lib/tools/ tool registrar (glob-discovered *.tool.js)
description:
## Why

Implements C6. A single `tool()` factory makes every tool a uniform
record: name, description, input/output Zod schemas, and a handler.
The registry discovers tools by scanning `api/lib/tools/*.tool.js`,
each of which default-exports a ToolDescriptor — so adding a tool only
requires creating a new file. No shared-file coordination. Both
adapters (HTTP, MCP) consume the same registry.

## Acceptance criteria

1. discoverTools returns one ToolDescriptor per *.tool.js file with stable ordering (alphabetic)
2. Files NOT ending in `.tool.js` are ignored (so helpers/fixtures coexist)
3. Duplicate tool name (post-discovery) throws (fail-fast)
4. File-name vs tool-name mismatch throws at discover time
5. createRegistry.invoke() validates input and output via the tool's Zod schemas; mismatches throw typed errors with ZodIssues

## Files in scope

- `api/lib/tools/registrar.js`
- `api/lib/tools/tool.js`
- `api/lib/tools/discover.js`
- `api/lib/tools/registrar.test.js`
- `api/lib/tools/discover.test.js`

## Out of scope

- Specific tool implementations (next four items — each is a separate *.tool.js)
- Adapter implementations (later items)
- Hot-reload of tool files (rebuild on file-add is acceptable for v1)

## API: new exports

- `tool({ name, description, input: ZodSchema, output: ZodSchema, handler }) -> ToolDescriptor`
- `createRegistry({ tools: ToolDescriptor[] }) -> { getTool(name), listTools(), invoke(name, input) }`
- `discoverTools({ cwd?, dir? }) -> Promise<ToolDescriptor[]>  // globs api/lib/tools/*.tool.js`

## Test plan

- discover.test.js — fixture dir with 3 *.tool.js files + 1 helper → asserts 3 discovered, ordering, dup-name throws, name-mismatch throws
- registrar.test.js — invoke happy path, input-validation failure, output-validation failure, unknown tool

## Risk

Low — pure scaffolding.

## Rollback

Revert PR; nothing depends on it yet.

---

acceptance_criteria: 1) discoverTools returns one ToolDescriptor per *.tool.js file with stable ordering (alphabetic) · 2) Files NOT ending in `.tool.js` are ignored (so helpers/fixtures coexist) · 3) Duplicate tool name (post-discovery) throws (fail-fast) · 4) File-name vs tool-name mismatch throws at discover time · 5) createRegistry.invoke() validates input and output via the tool's Zod schemas; mismatches throw typed errors with ZodIssues

title: Replace polling with SSE progress bus for extrapolation runs
description:
## Why

Implements C7. Today the frontend polls a status endpoint, which is both
noisy and lossy on stage transitions. SSE gives push-based progress with
one event per stage start/finish plus an optional partial-payload event
for incremental UX.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Subscribers receive every emitted event in order, even when subscribed mid-run (replay of past events from in-memory ring)
2. Stream emits 'run:end' once and closes the SSE connection cleanly
3. Heartbeat comment line every 15s to keep proxies happy

## Files in scope

- `api/lib/extrapolation/orchestrator.js`
- `api/lib/extrapolation/progress-bus.js`
- `api/lib/extrapolation/progress-bus.test.js`
- `api/routes/extrapolation/stream.js`
- `api/routes/extrapolation/stream.routes.test.js`

## Out of scope

- Frontend wiring (next item)
- Removing the polling endpoint (kept as fallback; deprecation in Phase 6)

## API: new exports

- `createProgressBus() -> { emit(event), subscribe(cb) -> unsub, close() }`

## API: new routes

- `GET /api/extrapolation/:runId/stream  -> text/event-stream`

## Test plan

- progress-bus.test.js — fanout to multiple subscribers, mid-run subscribe replays, idempotent close
- stream.routes.test.js — supertest with EventSource shim, asserts ordered events and clean close

## Risk

Medium — long-lived connections; ensure no leaks in tests.

## Rollback

Revert PR; polling endpoint remains.

---
*spec_id: `arch.phase4.progress-bus-sse` · phase: 4 · est_days: 1*
acceptance_criteria: 1) Subscribers receive every emitted event in order, even when subscribed mid-run (replay of past events from in-memory ring) · 2) Stream emits 'run:end' once and closes the SSE connection cleanly · 3) Heartbeat comment line every 15s to keep proxies happy

  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  era_entity_id TEXT,
  active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  payload_json TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

**SQL migration:** api/lib/db/migrations/2026-05-add-projects.sql

Medium — schema migration on existing data. The backfill default project is critical for not orphaning existing rows.

title: Vite-plugin mount point with glob-based route discovery
description:
## Why

Implements C8 skeleton. Instead of a hand-maintained _registry.js (which
would force every route-adding item to edit one shared file and create a
merge-conflict hotspot), the plugin discovers routes by globbing
`api/routes/**/*.route.js`. Each route file default-exports a
`{ method, path, handler, allowedModes? }` (or `register(app)`) descriptor.
Adding a new route only requires creating a new file — no shared-file
coordination. This is the file-isolation invariant for every later route
item in the spec.

## Acceptance criteria

1. vite.config.js imports qpbDevServer from './api/vite-plugin/index.js'
2. qpbDevServer is added to the plugins array; dev server starts without errors with an empty api/routes/ tree
3. discoverRoutes returns one entry per *.route.js file found, with stable ordering (alphabetic by path)
4. Duplicate path+method across discovered files throws a build-time error (fail-fast)
5. Adding a new file under api/routes/ that does NOT end in `.route.js` is ignored (so test helpers and utils can coexist)
6. All existing /api/* routes still respond identically via the inline middlewares (registry coexists; nothing migrated yet)

## Files in scope

- `api/vite-plugin/index.js`
- `api/vite-plugin/route-discovery.js`
- `api/vite-plugin/index.test.js`
- `api/vite-plugin/route-discovery.test.js`
- `api/routes/.gitkeep`
- `vite.config.js`

## Out of scope

- Migrating any existing route (Phase 6 work)
- Removing inline middlewares (Phase 6)
- Live reload on route-file add/remove during dev (rebuild on file-add is acceptable for v1)

## API: new exports

- `discoverRoutes({ cwd? }) -> Promise<RouteDescriptor[]>  // globs api/routes/**/*.route.js`
- `qpbDevServer({ env?, routesDir? }) -> VitePlugin`

## Test plan

- route-discovery.test.js — fixture dir with 3 *.route.js files + 1 non-route file → asserts the 3 are discovered and ordered; duplicate path/method throws
- index.test.js — feed a fake discovery result with one route, assert it's mounted on a fake server.middlewares stub
- Manual smoke after merge: curl /api/comfy-status, /api/character-bank, /api/entities

## Risk

Medium — vite.config.js change; if the plugin throws, dev server fails to start. Duplicate-detection prevents silent route collisions.

## Rollback

Revert vite.config.js to prior commit; api/routes/* + api/vite-plugin/* are orphans (safe).

4. System prompt for descriptor generation (this is critical — get it right):

'You are a casting director writing a concise visual description for a film production call sheet. Given a character profile, produce a 15-25 word description that includes ONLY:
- Age and gender presentation
- The 2-3 most visually distinctive physical features (face structure, hair, eyes, build)
- One clothing item if it is a signature element

description:
Before writing anything, use Serena to understand the current state. Find and read:

## P1-AUDIT findings

### 1. Characters table schema
- Base table from `api/lib/db/schema.js` `CREATE_TABLES_SQL` (lines 0-140): `id, project_id, embedding_status, payload_json, created_at, updated_at`.
- Shadow columns added via `MIGRATIONS` (lines 142-168): `archived_at, lifecycle_status, last_rendered_at, name, age, gender_presentation, cinematic_archetype` plus indexes.
- Migrations applied via `api/lib/db/sqlite.js:initializeDatabase` (try/catch each — idempotent).
- **P1-SCHEMA must append:** `ALTER TABLE characters ADD COLUMN prompt_descriptor TEXT`, `ALTER TABLE characters ADD COLUMN slug TEXT`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_characters_slug ON characters(slug)`.

### 2. payload_json structure (CharacterProfileSchema)
- Defined at `api/lib/characters/schemas.js:22-59` (zod, `.strict()`).
- Fields: id, projectId, name, age, apparentAgeRange, genderPresentation, ethnicityOrRegionalLook, faceShape, eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, jawline, cheekbones, skinTone, skinTexture, hairColor, hairLength, hairTexture, hairstyle, bodyType, heightImpression, posture, distinctiveFeatures, wardrobeBase, cinematicArchetype, personalityEnergy, visualKeywords, forbiddenSimilarities, qwenPromptSeed, embeddingStatus, createdAt, updatedAt, approved, lifecycleStatus, lastRenderedAt.
- **CRITICAL — `.strict()` constraint:** Unknown fields are REJECTED. To persist `slug` and `promptDescriptor` inside payload_json, they must be added to `CharacterProfileSchema` as optional fields. Alternative: store ONLY as DB columns and strip before validation (like `archived_at` does at `parseCharacterProfile:121-125`).
- **Decision:** Add both as optional zod fields on the schema — the brief explicitly says "Save the generated descriptor to the character record (both the prompt_descriptor column and inside payload_json)". Same for slug for consistency.

### 3. Path A — auditionOrchestrator.js
- `runAudition({ db, bankEntryId, count, views, workflowId, llmGenerate, comfyService })` at `api/lib/audition/auditionOrchestrator.js:14-171`.
- LLM produces a profile, then `parseCharacterProfile(candidatePayload)` validates, then `createCharacter(db, validated)` persists.
- **P1-SLUGS hook point:** after `parseCharacterProfile`, before `createCharacter` — compute slug from `candidatePayload.name`, ensure DB-side uniqueness, set on payload.
- **P1-AUTOGEN hook point:** after the for-loop's `createCharacter(db, validated)` succeeds (or after `runAudition` returns), fire descriptor generation per character.

### 4. Path B — batchReview.js
- `saveCandidateAsCharacter({ db, vectorStore, embeddingProvider }, payload)` at `api/lib/characters/batchReview.js:140-172`.
- Similarity check → `saveApprovedCandidateAsCharacter(db, parsed.candidateId)` (which lives in `api/lib/db/repositories.js:633-650`, NOT in batchReview.js as the brief states).
- `saveApprovedCandidateAsCharacter` reads candidate, calls `createCharacter(db, { ...candidateRecord.candidate, embeddingStatus, lifecycleStatus })`.
- **P1-SLUGS hook point:** Either inside `saveApprovedCandidateAsCharacter` (before createCharacter) or in `saveCandidateAsCharacter` — adding slug to the candidate payload before save.
- **P1-AUTOGEN hook point:** after `saveApprovedCandidateAsCharacter` returns successfully in `saveCandidateAsCharacter`. Existing fire-and-forget already lives at line 169 (`triggerReindex(...).catch(() => {})`) — replicate that exact pattern.

### 5. ActorDetail.jsx layout
- File: `src/components/ActorBank/ActorDetail.jsx`.
- Sections (in order): topBar (back button + Open in Casting Room + Archive/Restore) → hero (name + meta `age · gender · archetype`) → optional re-queue banner → Reference images section → Character profile section (PROFILE_SECTIONS map).
- **P1-UI insertion point:** New `<section className={styles.section}>` for "Prompt Descriptor", placed **between hero and Reference images** (line ~278) so it's visually prominent above the image strip. Uses existing `styles.section` / `styles.sectionTitle` patterns.
- Existing rename pattern (lines 233-251) is a useful template for inline edit (input + onBlur + onKeyDown for Enter/Escape).

### 6. polishCore.js LLM integration pattern
- `SYSTEM_PROMPT` at `api/lib/polishCore.js:11-98` — for prompt-polishing, not reused for descriptor.
- `runPolish({ payload, fetchImpl, env })` at lines 331-366: calls `buildUserMessage`, then `resolveProviderSelection`, then `runWithResolvedProvider`.
- `resolveProviderSelection({ engine, localOnly, fetchImpl, env, payload })` at lines 249-301: handles auto/embedded/local/cloud routing.
- `runWithResolvedProvider({ provider, userMessage, payload, fetchImpl, env, systemPrompt })` at lines 303-329: dispatches to provider-specific function with `systemPrompt` parameter — this is the key hook for our custom descriptor SYSTEM_PROMPT.
- **P1-API reuse pattern:** Import `resolveProviderSelection` and `runWithResolvedProvider` from polishCore. Build our own user message (the character profile fields). Call `resolveProviderSelection({ engine: 'auto', ... })`, then `runWithResolvedProvider({ ..., systemPrompt: DESCRIPTOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT })`. The `systemPrompt` parameter is already plumbed through to all providers.

### 7. slugify.js utilities
- `toSnakeSlug(input)` at `src/utils/slugify.js:3-9`: lowercase, non-alphanumeric → `_`, trim leading/trailing `_`.
- `withUniqueSuffix(baseSlug, characters, currentName)` at lines 14-29: takes an in-memory `characters` bucket (object keyed by slug). For DB-side uniqueness, this won't work directly — we'll need to either (a) load all existing slugs into a bucket first, or (b) loop with a DB existence query. The bucket approach is fine because the slug list is small.
- `resolveCharacterSlug(slug, characters)` at lines 34-46: handles snake/dash equivalence. Useful for @slug expansion in P3.
- **Note:** These are frontend utilities (src/utils/) but plain JS — they can be imported in API code too.

### 8. Fire-and-forget background pattern
- The brief references `backgroundCompilePromptPacks` — **this function does not exist in the codebase** (only in archived docs).
- The actual canonical fire-and-forget pattern is at `api/lib/characters/batchReview.js:169`:
  ```js
  triggerReindex(db, updated.savedCharacterId, { vectorStore, embeddingProvider }).catch(() => {})
  ```
- `triggerReindex` is defined at `api/lib/characterLifecycle.js:33-35` — a thin async wrapper around `indexCharacterById`.
- **P1-AUTOGEN pattern:** After `createCharacter` succeeds in both paths, call `generateDescriptorForCharacter(db, character.id, { env, fetchImpl }).catch((err) => console.warn('descriptor autogen failed', err))` — fire-and-forget, never throws to caller.

### Additional findings (not in brief but relevant)
- **`updateCharacter`** at `api/lib/db/repositories.js:157-196` is the canonical patch function. Merges patch onto current profile, validates via `parseCharacterProfile`, writes columns + payload_json. P1-UI's [Edit] button should POST to a new generic update route (or extend `/api/character-rename` to accept additional fields) and call `updateCharacter(db, id, { promptDescriptor: trimmed })`.
- **CharacterProfileSchema is `.strict()`** — both `slug` and `promptDescriptor` MUST be added as `.optional()` zod fields, otherwise every save will throw "Unrecognized key" errors.
- **Backfill hook:** `initializeDatabase` only runs MIGRATIONS (DDL). Data backfill (P1-BACKFILL-SLUGS) needs a separate function called after `initializeDatabase` from the same caller. The DB is created via `createSqliteDatabase` + `initializeDatabase` — find call sites in vite.config.js / api handlers and add `runOneTimeBackfills(db)` after.

title: P2-PERSIST: Update share URL and workspace profile encoding for new chars shape
description:
The share URL encodes chars state as part of the base64 JSON hash. Workspace profiles also save chars state. Both need to handle the expanded shape.

Share URL encoding:
- Use Serena to find the share URL encode/decode logic in App.jsx
- When encoding: include actorBankId, name, promptDescriptor for each char slot that has an Actor Bank character. Do NOT include thumbnailUrl
- When decoding: if actorBankId is present but other fields are missing, fetch from GET /api/characters/slugs on mount to fill in promptDescriptor and thumbnailUrl
- If actorBankId references a character that no longer exists, fall back to anonymous mode for that slot (clear actorBankId, keep g and a)

Workspace profiles:
- Use Serena to find how workspace profiles save and restore chars state
- Apply the same encoding/decoding logic as share URLs
- On profile restore: validate that referenced actorBankIds still exist

Add version field to share URL encoding if not already present (check if improvementSuggestions2.md M5 was implemented). If version exists, increment it. If not, add v: 2 and treat any decoded object without a v field as v: 1 (legacy, anonymous-only chars).
close_reason: Bumped CURRENT_SHARE_VERSION to 2. encodeShareState now sanitizes chars via sanitizeCharsForShare (drops thumbnailUrl per brief — recoverable from /api/characters/slugs cache). Decode keeps actorBankId+name+promptDescriptor in addition to g/a. Added a hydration useEffect that watches bankCharsForSelector + chars: fills in missing fields from the lookup AND clears stale actorBankIds for characters that no longer exist (deleted/archived). Settles in one cycle (setChars returns prev when nothing changes). Workspace profile restore goes through the same setChars path, so it benefits from the same reconciliation. All 317 tests pass; build succeeds.

title: P1-AUTOGEN: Auto-generate prompt descriptors on character creation
description:
When a character is created (both Path A and Path B), auto-generate a prompt descriptor in the background using the endpoint from P1-API. This should be non-blocking — the character creation succeeds even if descriptor generation fails.

Pattern: after createCharacter() returns successfully, fire a background call to POST /api/character-prompt-descriptor with the new character's ID.

NOTE: The brief references `backgroundCompilePromptPacks` as a pattern to copy, but that exact function name does not exist in the codebase. Use the equivalent fire-and-forget pattern identified during P1-AUDIT (likely a setImmediate / Promise.resolve().then() pattern near runAudition or saveCandidateAsCharacter).

Add this background call in both:
1. Path A: auditionOrchestrator.js / runAudition, after character creation
2. Path B: saveCandidateAsCharacter in batchReview.js, after character creation

The background task must catch and log errors — never throw to the caller.
close_reason: Wired fire-and-forget descriptor generation in both creation paths. Path A: auditionOrchestrator.js after createCharacter() inside the per-profile loop. Path B: batchReview.js saveCandidateAsCharacter() after the existing triggerReindex() block. Both use the canonical .catch(err => console.warn(...)) pattern so descriptor failures never propagate. All 198 tests pass.

title: P1-BACKFILL-SLUGS: Backfill slugs for existing characters
description:
Write a one-time backfill script that runs on app startup (alongside existing migrations in sqlite.js or schema.js).

Query all characters where slug IS NULL. For each:
1. Extract name from payload_json
2. Compute slug via toSnakeSlug(name)
3. If slug collides with an existing slug, use withUniqueSuffix()
4. UPDATE the slug column

This should run once and be idempotent — if all characters already have slugs, it does nothing.

Use Serena to find where migrations run (the initDb or ensureSchema function) to know where to hook this in.
close_reason: Added backfillCharacterSlugs to api/lib/db/sqlite.js, called from initializeDatabase via runDataBackfills wrapper. Queries characters WHERE slug IS NULL, derives slug from payload_json.name, ensures uniqueness against existing slugs and within-batch picks, updates both slug column and payload_json. Idempotent (does nothing if all slugs are populated). All 198 tests pass.

title: H1: Stop overwriting classification field on batch candidate approve/reject
description: When a batch candidate is approved or rejected, both review_status AND classification are updated to 'approved'/'accepted' or 'rejected'. These are independent signals: classification = system automated assessment, review_status = user decision. Fix: in approve/reject/reconsider handlers, only update review_status. title: Integrate Chroma auto-spawn into dev server startup
description:
## Why This Issue Exists

Running chroma run --path ./chroma_data manually before starting the dev server is easy to forget. The vector features (batch similarity, indexing) fail silently until Chroma is up.

## What Was Done

- vite.config.js: startChromaServer() spawns system Python chroma on server listen. Detects already-running instance via /api/v2/heartbeat (v1 fallback). Strips node_modules/.bin from PATH to avoid the chromadb npm CLI (which doesn't support Windows x64). Uses cmd /c on Windows, sh -c on Unix to avoid shell:true deprecation warning. Kills process on exit/SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- GET /api/chroma-health middleware added to vite.config.js dev plugin.
- src/lib/api/comfy.js: getChromaHealth() added.
- CastingPipelinePanel.jsx: chromaReady state + useEffect polling every 3s until ready then every 30s.
- Status badge next to 'Casting Room' heading: pulsing dot + 'Chroma starting...' → solid green 'Chroma ready'.
- CSS: titleRow, chromaBadge, chromaBadgeReady, chromaBadgeStarting, chromaDot, chromaPulse animation.
close_reason: Implemented: Chroma auto-spawns on npm run dev via vite.config.js configureServer hook. Health endpoint at /api/chroma-health. Frontend badge in Casting Room header polls every 3s until ready then 30s. Handles already-running, Windows x64 CLI conflict, and process cleanup on exit.

title: H3: Move ComfyUI job lists from sessionStorage to SQLite
description:
## Why This Issue Exists

Active ComfyUI job lists are stored in sessionStorage. A full portfolio render takes 30-45 minutes. If the browser is closed during this time, sessionStorage is wiped. ComfyUI continues rendering but the app never ingests completed images when the user returns. The only recovery is the Developer Tools 'Ingest Outputs' button, which most users won't find.

## What Needs to Be Done

1. Create comfy_jobs table (migration):
   - id TEXT PRIMARY KEY
   - prompt_id TEXT NOT NULL
   - character_id TEXT NOT NULL
   - view_type TEXT NOT NULL
   - job_type TEXT NOT NULL ('audition' | 'portfolio' | 'preview' | 'more_takes')
   - status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued'
   - created_at TEXT NOT NULL
   - completed_at TEXT

2. On app load (Casting Room mount): query for all non-terminal jobs (status NOT IN ('success', 'failed')). If any exist, resume polling automatically. Show RenderStatusBar immediately.

3. Remove all sessionStorage reads/writes for job lists.

## Serena Usage

close_reason: ComfyUI job persistence migrated from sessionStorage to SQLite comfy_jobs table; full backend + frontend wired

title: Generate Previews should target only approved candidates, not pending

What needs to be done:
- Change the targets filter in handleGeneratePreviews from:

    candidates.filter((c) => c.reviewStatus === 'approved' && !batchPreviewJobs[c.id])
- Update the button disabled condition to match: disabled when no approved candidates remain unqueued.
- If no candidates are approved yet, show a hint near the button: 'Cast characters first, then generate previews.'

title: Debug: LM Studio audition timeout — fix JSON mode, max_tokens, thinking suppression
description:
User hits 'Local LM Studio request timed out' when pressing Generate Audition. Root causes identified:

1. **Thinking mode not properly suppressed**: lmStudioProvider sends /no_think as text prefix, but LM Studio 0.3+ supports enable_thinking=false API param for Qwen3 models. If the GGUF lacks the /no_think token, the model does full CoT reasoning and burns through max_tokens before outputting JSON — causing 120s timeout.

2. **max_tokens=2000 too low for audition**: 3 candidates × 15+ fields each = ~2500-3500 tokens of JSON. Model hits ceiling mid-output; LM Studio may hang or truncate silently.

3. **response_format not forwarded**: providerPayload carries responseFormat:'json' from auditionOrchestrator but lmStudioProvider ignores it. LM Studio supports response_format:{type:'json_object'} for constrained JSON output — without it the model may wrap output in markdown fences breaking parseJsonFromLlmText.

4. **No debug logging**: When timeout fires there is no trace of what was sent or how long it ran — impossible to diagnose further without adding request/response logging.

Fixes needed:
- Add enable_thinking:false to request body when LMSTUDIO_NO_THINK is true (LM Studio native suppression)
- Honor responseFormat:'json' by adding response_format:{type:'json_object'} to request body  
- Increase default max_tokens to 4000 (configurable via LMSTUDIO_MAX_TOKENS env var already exists)
- Add console.error/warn logging in lmStudioProvider for request start, response time, and errors
